label: D2: rare a1->S2 transition following a rewarded trial
explanation: Fires only at D2 (never at D1 or GO), and essentially only when the agent chose a1 and landed in S2, i.e. a rare transition after a1 (99.3% recall, 99.8% of mass for a1&S2 at D2; almost nothing on a2->S1 rare, and nothing on common transitions). Adding prev_reward == 1 (the previous trial was rewarded, which is observed) raises precision from 0.58 to 0.80, giving dev F1 0.85 with mass recall 0.96. Activations it misses after an unrewarded previous trial are weak (about 0.1-0.4 of max), so a prior reward raises magnitude. The remaining false positives are mostly a1->S2R trials where the agent had been choosing a2 or switching, consistent with the feature being strongest when the agent holds an S1-good belief (good == 1 carries 87% of mass). It does not fire on a2 choices, S1 arrivals, or common transitions. All variables are observable at D2.

issues: The basic claims hold. All activation is at D2 (0 active steps at D1 and GO). a1->S2 rare carries 99.8% of activation mass, and a2->S1 rare and common transitions carry about 0.2%. prev_reward==1 carries 96.6% of mass. The original predicate's test scores reproduce: P 0.791, R 0.906, F1 0.845, mass recall 0.961.

Systematic false-positive class: when the previous trial was rewarded in S2, the feature never fires. The predicate's part with prev_state==2 has precision 0.000 on both splits (1487 dev steps, 1637 test steps), which is about 25% of all test false positives. So 'following a rewarded trial' overclaims. The feature only follows a reward collected in S1 (or one whose state is outside the window).
Adding (prev_state != 2) loses no recall and raises precision. Dev: P 0.842, R 0.916, F1 0.878. Test: P 0.836, R 0.906, F1 0.870, mass recall 0.961.

The remaining false positives are mostly a1->S2 rare trials with unrewarded or rare-S2 trials earlier in the history. Requiring 2-back conditions (tv('reward',-2)!=0 or tv('state',-2)!=2) raises precision only to about 0.85 and costs about 15% recall, so I treat this as weaker graded modulation, not a clean class.
The missed activations are weak (about 0.1-0.4 of max) and are mostly a1->S2 rare trials after an unrewarded previous trial, as the original explanation said. They hold 3.6% of mass.
skeptic.revised_label: D2: rare a1->S2 transition when the previous trial was rewarded in S1 (silent if the previous reward came from S2)
